name: Seeing the Unseen: Instruments That Opened the Universe
description: Lenses, rays, magnets and lasers: how scientists built tools to see the very far and the very small, and what those tools found.

checkpoints.name: Old tools
checkpoints.note: The astrolabe measured the heights of stars, Ibn al-Haytham worked out how the eye and lenses behave, and lens grinders in Europe made the first spectacles and, around 1590, microscopes.

checkpoints.name: The lens revolution
checkpoints.note: Galileo turned a telescope to the sky, Leeuwenhoek and Hooke found tiny living things and cells with microscopes, and the thermometer and barometer made weather and heat measurable.

checkpoints.name: Rays and cells
checkpoints.note: Cell theory made the microscope central to biology. In 1895 X-rays showed bones through flesh, a hint that unseen radiation could be harnessed.

checkpoints.name: Particles and radio skies
checkpoints.note: Geiger counters, electron microscopes and cyclotrons probed atoms. Radio telescopes found pulsars, found by Jocelyn Bell, and the cosmic microwave background, and CERN gave Europe a shared accelerator.

checkpoints.name: Giant machines
checkpoints.note: CT and MRI scanners look inside the living body, the Hubble and James Webb telescopes look back to early galaxies, the Large Hadron Collider found the Higgs boson, and LIGO's detectors heard gravitational waves from colliding black holes.
